title: Compose output and cost for the same subroutine execution
obstacle: The caller needs both a mathematical output and a resource bound, but the proposed component specifications describe different computations.
procedure: Identify the subroutine actually invoked and the inputs passed by its caller.
Consider one specification connecting its execution, output representation and cost. Include state preservation only for data still needed by a consumer.
Compose the proved specification through the actual calling convention and include any required conversion overhead.
verification: Instantiate the contract at a real call and verify that the output used by the next step came from the execution whose cost was bounded.
positive_example: A proved scan returns its computed sum and bounds the operations on that input, allowing an outer loop to reuse both facts.
negative_example: Adding a cost field to a successful result without showing how the executed program produces that cost leaves the resource claim open.

evidence.note: General design guidance. Check its conditions in the current argument; no comparative performance claim.
